title: Rationalize entity associations & mitigate control-plane hot-query paths
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: The control plane is suffering from several interrelated schema anti-patterns: polymorphic foreign keys across tenant and project entities, wide join-heavy views that frequently touch hot rows, and duplicated ownership refs that inflate row width. These induce costly query plans during tenant list and project read paths, raising p95 latency and causing occasional KV cache thrashing. This ticket scopes a focused refactor: introduce compact association tables, add covering indexes for common read paths, and implement an online migration strategy (shadow tables + backfill + cutover) to avoid large locks.
acceptance_criteria: Primary read paths for tenant/project listing have p95 latency reduced by >=30% in staging
No > 10s exclusive locks during any online migration in canary runs
Shadow association tables fully backfilled and verified with checksum queries
New indexes do not regress write latency by more than 5% on the control-plane write benchmarks
Migration runbook and rollback steps documented with sample queries and required RBAC/roles
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Analyze hot queries - collect EXPLAIN ANALYZE samples for tenant_list, project_fetch, and membership joins; identify plans that cause nested loop/hash join amplification
Phase 2: Design compact associations - introduce 'entity_assoc' narrow table (tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id, owner_id, created_at) to replace 2-3 polymorphic FK patterns
Phase 3: Shadow tables & backfill - create shadow_entity_assoc, backfill in batches with idempotent workers, maintain a sync gap using 'updated_since' watermark
Phase 4: Indexing - add covering indexes (tenant_id, owner_id, entity_type) and partial indexes for common predicates; validate index sizes and selectivity on staging data sample
Phase 5: Swap reads - add feature flag-controlled read routing (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%), compare checksums and latency metrics; run consistency checks across a 24h window
Phase 6: Cutover and cleanup - after 72h of stable canary, flip write paths, deprecate legacy columns, and schedule eventual schema pruning with a 90-day TTL for old refs
Rollback plan: if checksum or latency regression observed at any canary stage, stop routing, switch reads back, pause backfill workers, and run fast diff queries to reconcile partial backfills

Monitoring: add dashboard tiles - p95 latency, 99th percentile lock wait, index hit ratio, backfill lag, and checksum mismatch rate; add alerts for >1% checksum mismatch or p95 latency regression >15%
Migration safety: all DDLs to be executed with CREATE TABLE AS and index builds concurrently where supported; avoid ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN in same window as heavy writes
Coordination: schedule DB maintenance windows for final index build steps and prune operations; communicate to Platform and SRE teams via #platform-db with links to runbook
